summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a man with chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and a history of alcohol dependence, was admitted for alcohol withdrawal, chest pain, and an untreated pulmonary embolism from a prior admission where he left against medical advice. He presented with confusion, dizziness, right ankle pain from a recent fall, and neuropathic chest and shoulder pain. During his stay, he was treated for alcohol withdrawal with benzodiazepines, restarted on heart failure and anticoagulation therapy, and diagnosed with B12 deficiency and BPPV. He initially refused treatment and showed signs of depression and impaired decision-making, prompting a psychiatric evaluation and temporary legal intervention. Over time, he regained capacity, agreed to treatment, and was discharged to a shelter with a comprehensive medication plan including daily enoxaparin, oral B12, and plans for outpatient follow-up for mental health and substance use.
problems: Major depressive affective disorder, single episode, unspecified
Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Other sprains and strains of ankle
Unspecified hereditary and idiopathic peripheral neuropathy
Automatic implantable cardiac defibrillator in situ
